title: Strategy

act2.summary: a fourth policy, and the policy name now arrives from a config file an operator can typo

solutions.title: Policy objects behind a ranking interface
solutions.tradeoff: A new policy is one new file and one line of registration. The price: reading the whole night plan now means opening the packer and one policy, and a policy can only express itself as a total ordering - a policy that needs to look at what is already scheduled does not fit the interface.

reviewFocus: Is the packing invariant (horizon, budget, start minutes, skipped) in exactly one place, or did it get copied into the policies?
Does the strategy interface express the varying axis only - ordering - or did packing leak into it?
Are the policy names owned by one place, so the error message and the dispatch cannot drift apart?
Does the git log show small steps with a green suite between them, or one commit called 'refactor'?
Is `rank` the right name for what the policy does, and would `order`, `sort` or `choose` have been better?
